\textbf{(a)} $x^3-3x^2+2x=x(x-1)(x-2)$ and $\dfrac{4-x}{x(x-1)(x-2)}=\dfrac2x-\dfrac3{x-1}+\dfrac1{x-2}$:
\[\Big[2\ln x-3\ln(x-1)+\ln(x-2)\Big]_3^4=2\ln\tfrac43-3\ln\tfrac32+\ln2=\boxed{8\ln2-5\ln3}\approx0.0521.\]
\textbf{(b)} Let $u=\sqrt x$, $du=\frac{dx}{2\sqrt x}$:
\[\int_1^\infty\frac{e^{-\sqrt x}}{\sqrt x}dx=\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_1^{\sqrt t}2e^{-u}du=\boxed{\frac2e}.\]

Measure $y$ up from the bottom ($0\le y\le10$). The cross-section has a flat bottom 42 ft long and a slope rising over 40 ft to the surface, so at height $y$ the water's length is $42+4y$ ft (82 ft at the top). A slice is $60(42+4y)\,dy$ ft$^3$ and is lifted $10-y$ ft to the top:
\[W=62.4\int_0^{10}60(42+4y)(10-y)\,dy=3744\int_0^{10}(420-2y-4y^2)\,dy=3744\Big(4200-100-\frac{4000}{3}\Big)=\boxed{10{,}358{,}400\ \text{ft-lb}}.\]
